### P15 Compute Shader · Compute

description: 2D plot of moving points with their velocity. xyBuffer holds a flat [x, y, x, y, ...] array (e.g. Arraygen -> Array to buffer, Float32); the index of each pair is the point's id, and each id gets its own colour (golden-ratio hue). Every point is drawn as a disc, and an arrow leaving it shows the velocity: direction = direction of motion, length = speed * velocityScale. Velocity is measured only w…; categories: Generator, Visualization; passes: 2; resources: xyBuffer:storage, state:storage, outputImage:image, inputMin:point2D, inputMax:point2D, yUp:bool, pointRadius:float, lineWidth:float, velocityScale:float, smoothing:float, staleTime:float, background:color

```glsl
// Pass 0 draws the plot: each pixel loops over the points (no write races).
// Pass 1 stores this frame's positions / velocities for the next frame.

const uint MAX_POINTS = 256u;

uint pointCount() { return min(uint(xyBuffer.points.length()), MAX_POINTS); }

// Smoothed velocity (input units / second) of point i at position p, from
// last frame's state. prevPos: xy = last *distinct* sample, z = 1 once the id
// exists, w = TIME of that sample. TIMEDELTA is not used: it is the gap
// between the last two scheduler ticks, not between rendered frames, so
// dividing a frame's displacement by it gives huge, erratic speeds.
vec2 currentVelocity(uint i, vec2 p)
{
  vec4 prev = state.prevPos[i];
  vec2 oldVel = state.velocity[i].xy;
  if(prev.z < 0.5)
    return vec2(0.0);                // new id: no history yet

  float dt = TIME - prev.w;
```
